entities.name: Givi Amilakhvari
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Givi Amilakhvari (1689–1754) was a Georgian nobleman (tavadi) with a prominent role in the politics of eastern Georgia in the first half of the 18th century.

He waged a lengthy struggle against the Ottoman and Iranian encroachments, changing sides and forging various alliances as he tried to preserve autonomy for his native kingdom of Kartli as well as to prevent the ascendant Bagrationi dynasty of the neighboring Georgian kingdom of Kakheti from seizing the throne of Kartli.

In the closing year of his life, Amilakhvari was forced to flee Kartli after the Russian Empire, which had been expanding its territory in the region, supported the Bagrationi dynasty.

Givi Amilakhvari's struggle against the Ottoman and Iranian empires had significant regional implications, shaping the political landscape of the Caucasus and contributing to the rise of Russian influence in the region.

A prominent figure in the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the politics of 18th-century Georgia, Amilakhvari's legacy has been largely overshadowed by the more prominent Bagrationi dynasty.

Despite this, his efforts to preserve Kartli's autonomy and resist the encroachment of foreign powers remain a testament to the resilience and determination of the Georgian people.
